behavioral_notes.observation: Questions and answers are the SAME model forum.post: a record with parent_id=False is a question, a record with parent_id set is an answer to that question (child_ids). Comments are mail.message records on the post (mail.thread), and convert_answer_to_comment / convert_comment_to_answer move content between the two representations. Not visible in metadata — the single self-referential model implements the whole Q&A tree.

Accepting an answer sets is_correct=True via write(); the override grants karma to BOTH parties (answer author gets forum.karma_gen_answer_accepted, default 15; acceptor gets forum.karma_gen_answer_accept, default 2) and refuses the action with AccessError unless user.karma >= karma_answer_accept_own/all. has_validated_answer on the question recomputes. Removing acceptance reverses the karma. This dual-karma side-effect lives only in Python.

behavioral_notes.element: forum.post karma-gated actions (vote / edit / close / comment / flag)
behavioral_notes.observation: _compute_post_karma_rights derives ~16 can_* booleans (can_ask, can_answer, can_edit, can_close, can_upvote, can_downvote, can_comment, can_flag, can_moderate...) by comparing the user's res.users.karma to per-forum thresholds (e.g. karma_edit_own=1 vs karma_edit_all=300, karma_close_own=100 vs karma_close_all=500, karma_upvote=5, karma_downvote=50, karma_flag=500, karma_moderate=1000). create()/write()/vote()/message_post() re-check these and raise AccessError. _update_content additionally strips links to rel=nofollow and blocks images/links below karma_dofollow/karma_editor. This permission-by-reputation model is entirely code-driven, invisible to metadata.

vote(upvote) creates/updates a forum.post.vote (Selection -1/0/1) for (post,user); vote_count is the stored sum of votes and drives relevancy (math.copysign time-decayed score) and the default _order 'is_correct DESC, vote_count DESC, last_activity_date DESC'. Casting a vote triggers karma generation on the post author (karma_gen_question_upvote=5, karma_gen_answer_upvote=10, downvotes negative). The voting->reputation->ranking loop is the core network mechanic and is not metadata-derivable.

state in {active, pending, close, offensive, flagged}. New questions from users below karma_post (default 100) are forced to 'pending' and routed to moderators via message_post_with_source (validation_queue); validate() activates and awards the deferred 'ask question' karma. close()/_mark_as_offensive()/_flag()/_refuse() move posts through the queue and apply karma penalties (karma_gen_answer_flagged=-100, x10 for a spammer's first post). _notify_state_update posts threaded notifications to followers and tag-followers. None of this workflow is in metadata.

Module inherits gamification.challenge (adds challenge_category='forum') and gamification.karma.tracking, and ships ~29 gamification.badge records across 4 data files: question (Student, Nice/Good/Great Question, Popular/Notable/Famous Question, Scholar...), answer (Teacher, Nice/Good/Great Answer, Enlightened, Guru, Self-Learner), participation (Autobiographer, Commentator, Pundit, Taxonomist...), moderation (Cleanup, Critic, Editor, Supporter...). Badges are awarded by gamification challenges evaluating karma/activity domains — the gamification engine, not website_forum metadata, computes them.

controllers/website_forum.py extends website_profile.WebsiteProfile and exposes ~40 /forum/* routes (browse/ask/answer/vote/accept/close/flag/validation queues/user profile). forum.post._get_microdata emits schema.org QAPage / Question / Answer JSON-LD (acceptedAnswer + suggestedAnswer) for SEO; _get_related_posts runs a raw-SQL Jaccard tag-similarity query. These behaviors are static/code-read, not in Python field metadata.

17 JS files, 6 XML templates, 2 OWL components (FlagMarkAsOffensiveDialog, WebsiteForumTagsWrapper); 5 registry registrations (4 public.interactions for website_forum/share/spam/profile-activity + 1 view website_forum_add_form); patches NewContentSystrayItem.prototype (adds 'Forum Post' to the website New-content menu); asset bundles include web.assets_frontend (7), website.assets_editor, web.assets_backend.

classification.apqc_category: 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services
classification.rationale: Value model = network (Stabell & Fjeldstad): website_forum is mediating technology — it links members who want to be interdependent (askers seeking answers, answerers seeking reputation) and creates value by enabling and orchestrating their exchanges, not by transforming inputs (chain) or matching a problem to a stored solution (shop). The value of the platform rises with the size and activity of the community and the accumulated content: the self-referential forum.post question/answer tree, the vote/karma/badge reputation loop, and tag-based discovery are classic network-mediation infrastructure (membership via auth_signup, capacity utilisation via relevancy/ranking). Activity class = primary: the forum is the customer-facing value-producing asset itself (a public website property), not an internal enabling function. APQC = 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services: the manifest category is Website/Website and the out-of-box default welcome message frames the forum as a marketing/community-engagement asset ('build your professional profile and become a better marketer together') — it drives SEO (schema.org QAPage microdata), brand community, top-of-funnel engagement and lead capture (auth_signup), which sit under Market-and-Sell rather than transactional sales. NOTE: an equally defensible mapping is 6.0 Manage Customer Service (specifically self-service / community knowledge-base deflection) when the forum is deployed as post-sale peer support; chosen 3.0 because the default framing, Website category, and SEO/community-marketing mechanics weight it toward marketing/community engagement rather than ticketed service.
